premiseCorrection.filedAs: fixtures are placed for the old 7 m parametric box; make placement derive from the generated room's measured bounds
premiseCorrection.measuredVerdict: HALF FALSE, and the half that is false is the one that would have been built first
premiseCorrection.why: resolveWallAnchorPosition places a fixture's ORIGIN at plane -/+ wallInsetMeters. The offending overhang is the assembly's own extent about that origin MINUS the inset - 0.575 - 0.08 = 0.495 m for the board - and that expression contains no room dimension. Re-running the width maths against the generated room's 6.376 m still leaves the board 0.56 m outside. Proven by contract: wall-anchored-fixture-fit.test.ts 'anchors at the same distance from the wall in a small room as a large one'.
premiseCorrection.actualDefect: the board and door are authored facing +Z (width along X, thin along Z) and NOTHING ever rotated them, so a slot declaring wall '-x' rendered a panel lying ACROSS the left wall. It fails on the SHIPPED parametric box, in all 14 environments, before any generated room is involved: 24 offenders, a constant 0.575 m (board) and 0.100 m (door) at every room width.

wallFacingYawRadians(wall) derived from the identity that rotating by t maps +Z to (sin t, 0, cos t); WALL_BOARD gains facesWall: true. DOOR_LEAF deliberately does NOT - its own source comment makes it a free-standing entry assembly, and the parametric shell has no +Z wall.

rotationY on the build input; anchorFixtureNearFaceToPlane() slides a fixture along its wall normal until its NEAR FACE - read from its own world AABB - sits at wallInsetMeters from a given plane. No per-fixture constant.
